blocks.text: CyberAlchemy Lab × Craft Hackathon

Full event rules v{{RULES_VERSION}} | Updated {{RULES_UPDATED}}. Registration: {{REGISTRATION_OPEN}} to {{REGISTRATION_CLOSE}}. Project month: {{BUILD_OPEN}} to {{SUBMISSION_CLOSE}}. Final results: {{FINAL}}. Individual new projects; age {{MINIMUM_AGE}}+; one project in one category; one final ballot with at most one vote per category.
Purpose

The CyberAlchemy Lab × Craft Hackathon invites participants to create one new project using both Craft and CyberAlchemy Lab, entered in either Studio front-end or Open projects. Each category has one participant-chosen winner and one US$200 subscription prize.

Participants choose the winners through voting. Organizers check eligibility, apply the published rules, resolve documented irregularities, and deliver prizes; they do not replace the vote with a judging score.
Schedule and time zone
All dates are in {{EVENT_YEAR}} and use Brasília time, America/Sao_Paulo (UTC-3). Registration and the project month are separate periods. The schedule below replaces the v1.0 calendar.
Registration opens: {{REGISTRATION_OPEN}}. Registration and the final participant roster close: {{REGISTRATION_CLOSE}}.
Build kickoff: {{BUILD_OPEN}}. Eligible projects are created during the project month, ending {{SUBMISSION_CLOSE}}. Registration does not start the build period.
Project submissions close: {{SUBMISSION_CLOSE}}. Registration has already closed; only registered participants may submit.
Eligibility review and project gallery publication: before voting opens at {{VOTING_OPEN}}. The gallery separates entries into their two categories.
Voting opens: {{VOTING_OPEN}}. Voting closes: {{VOTING_CLOSE}}.
Provisional results: {{RESULTS}}. Reports of voting or eligibility errors are due by {{REPORT}}. Final selection and results are published by {{FINAL}}.
A form receipt timestamp determines whether a registration, submission, or ballot arrived on time. Starting a form before the deadline does not count as submitting it.
Individual participation
Participation is free. Participants must be at least 18 years old and able to receive the subscription prize in their location. No paid OpenAI subscription is required to enter.

Individual entries only. Each person may register once and submit one project in exactly one category. One person cannot submit an entry in both categories. Each project has one participating creator; team entries are not eligible.
Every participant registers using one Google Account that they control. Registration includes a display name, verified account email, and acceptance of these rules.

The participant roster is fixed at the registration deadline. The creator submits their own project and receives any prize on their own account. Event administrators who control submissions, ballots, or results are not eligible to compete or vote.

Every valid registered participant may vote, including registered builders who do not finish a submission. Only the finalized participant roster receives ballot access. Spectators and unregistered supporters may view the gallery but cannot vote.
Two categories

Studio front-end: develop a new front-end for a CyberAlchemy Lab / Craft Studio. Aim for a beautiful, wild and original UI whose new UX features favor human–machine ergonomics: help people understand the system, guide machines and work with less friction. Demonstrate working interactions, explain their intended ergonomic benefit and identify any simulated behavior honestly.

Open projects: the original challenge remains. Build an ambitious new project using Craft and CyberAlchemy Lab: agent companies, forkable worlds, learning systems, machine beliefs, tool invention, living art or your own idea. Pick one ambitious behavior and let participants try it.

Choose exactly one category in the final submission. A project competes only within that category; the same project cannot enter both. The common eligibility and submission requirements below apply to both categories.
Project eligibility

Only new projects created during the announced build period are eligible. Improvements to an existing project, previously completed entries, and resubmissions from earlier competitions are not eligible.

Projects must make substantive use of both Craft and CyberAlchemy Lab. The submission must identify what was used and demonstrate its role in the result; adding the names or logos alone is insufficient.

Libraries, frameworks, starter templates, public datasets, and AI assistance are allowed. Credit outside work, follow its license, and clearly identify the original contribution created for this hackathon. Repackaging an existing application as a new project is not eligible.
A working prototype is sufficient. Demonstrate the core behavior and state known limitations honestly. Ideas without a working demonstration are not eligible.
Participants supply their own tools and cover their own development, hosting, and API costs. Prize subscriptions are awarded after selection.
Required submission

The creator submits one entry containing: exactly one category (Studio front-end or Open projects); project title; a short description of the problem and intended user; their registered display name and account identifier; a project or repository link; and a demo video of up to three minutes.
Also include: an explanation of how Craft and the lab were used; instructions for accessing or running the prototype; attribution for reused assets and tools; and known limitations.
Include a stable snapshot of the submitted version, such as a commit hash, release tag, or dated export. The demo and evaluation must reflect that version.

Public source code is encouraged but not required. Organizers must have sufficient access to verify the prototype; the public demo and description must be accessible to all voters without paid access.

The creator may edit the submitted entry before the deadline. After the deadline, feature additions and replacement demos are excluded from evaluation. Organizers may permit a recorded correction to a broken link or access setting if it does not change the submitted work.
Do not include credentials, private personal data, or material you lack permission to disclose. An incomplete, inaccessible, late, or ineligible entry may be excluded, with a stated reason.
Gallery and voting
Organizers publish the eligible project gallery before voting begins. Each entry receives the same presentation fields and a stable project identifier. Votes remain private during voting.

Each registered participant may submit one final ballot with one project choice in each category, or abstain in either category. Each valid category choice has equal weight: one vote per participant per category.

Participants may not vote for a project they helped create. A self-vote is invalid for that category and does not earn a replacement choice. A valid choice in the other category can still count. Participants may abstain in either or both categories.

The ballot requires the participant’s registered Google Account. Access is restricted to the finalized roster, response editing is disabled, and the form accepts at most one response per authorized account.

Registering or voting through multiple accounts, impersonating another participant, automated ballots, buying votes, offering benefits in exchange for a vote, and organized vote-trading are prohibited. Sharing a project and asking eligible participants to consider it is allowed.

Platform controls limit submissions per authorized account; they do not independently prove one account belongs to one real person. Organizers therefore check the roster and examine documented duplicate or fraudulent registrations.

If a platform failure produces duplicate records for the same authorized participant, use the earliest on-time ballot from that account and assess each category choice independently. Later duplicates do not replace disallowed choices. Confirmed deliberate vote manipulation can invalidate the person’s ballots and disqualify an involved project where involvement is established. A project is not disqualified solely because an unaffiliated person tried to manipulate voting.
How winners are selected

In each category, the eligible project with the most valid votes wins that category’s prize. For Studio front-end, consider visual beauty and originality, inventive UX features, and human–machine ergonomics demonstrated through usable interactions. For Open projects, keep the original guidance: originality, usefulness, quality of the demonstrated prototype, and meaningful use of Craft and the lab. These are guidance for voters, not a separate organizer scoring system.

A category awards its prize only to an eligible project receiving at least one valid vote. If a category has no such project, its prize is unawarded and does not transfer to the other category or to organizers.

If a tie affects a category’s winning place, organizers conduct a recorded random draw among the tied projects in that category. The two categories are counted independently. No second voting round is held.

Organizers remove invalid ballots before calculating final totals. The published report lists valid votes per eligible project, the number of invalid ballots with summarized reasons, any disqualifications, and any tie-draw result. Individual voter identities and choices are not published.
Prizes and delivery

Two subscription prizes are available: one US$200 prize for the Studio front-end winner and one US$200 prize for the Open projects winner. The intended subscription is one month of ChatGPT Pro at the US$200 tier. Total organizer subscription funding remains US$400.
Each winning creator receives one subscription prize on their own account. The two winning projects belong to two different participants.

The prize is reimbursement of an eligible one-month ChatGPT Pro subscription at the US$200 tier, up to US$200 per winning project, against a valid receipt. The winner purchases the subscription on their own account. Winners must contact hello@cyberalchemize.com within seven calendar days of final results; reimbursement is completed within fourteen calendar days of receiving a valid receipt and agreed payment details.

The US$200 funding cap includes any applicable taxes, currency conversion, and payment fees. Any cost beyond the cap is the recipient’s responsibility. There is no funding for later subscription renewals.

No account credentials are shared. Continued subscription renewals are the recipient’s responsibility and are not included in the prize. No cash alternative or API-credit substitution is promised by these rules.

If a winning project is found ineligible before delivery, the next qualifying project in the same category receives the available prize, applying the same published vote and tie rules. Contact a nonresponding winner again before treating the prize as declined.
Ownership and event promotion
Participants retain ownership of their original work. Submission does not require transferring ownership or assigning an open-source license.

By submitting, participants grant CyberAlchemy Lab permission to display the submitted project title, description, creator display name, screenshots, and demo, with attribution, in the event gallery and materials promoting this hackathon and its results. This permission does not authorize relicensing or selling their project.
Participants are responsible for permission to use and share included third-party material. Private organizer access to code does not authorize public publication of that code.
Conduct, privacy, and disputes

Treat participants respectfully. Harassment, plagiarism, deliberate misrepresentation, unauthorized access to systems or data, and interference with another entry or the voting process can lead to removal, with a recorded reason.

Registration emails, ballot identities, reports, and payment details are restricted to the organizers who need them. Public gallery data is kept separate from the private registration and ballot records. Marketing email requires a separate opt-in.

Operational registration and identifiable voting records are deleted thirty days after prize delivery and dispute resolution. Records needed to document reimbursement may be kept separately. Aggregate results and the project gallery may remain public.

Reports go to hello@cyberalchemize.com. Include the project identifier, a description of the issue, and supporting evidence. A person affected by a disqualification can provide a response before final results are issued.

Organizers resolve eligibility, counting, and conduct disputes using these rules and publish any correction that changes the outcome. They may not choose a preferred project instead of applying the vote result.

Any unavoidable platform outage is announced to all participants with the same remedy for everyone affected. Rule changes must be published and highlighted. After the revised kickoff, the one-ballot/one-vote-per-category rule, equal category prizes and voting-based selection cannot be changed. If an outage makes the {{FINAL}} final-selection deadline impossible, announce that explicitly rather than publishing unchecked results.
Organizer and rules version
Organizer: CyberAlchemy Lab. Organizer contact: hello@cyberalchemize.com

The official event page carries registration and submission links, the full rules, and access links for Craft and CyberAlchemy Lab. Project-gallery and voting links follow after eligibility review. Questions, disputes, and prize claims go to the organizer contact above.

Rules version {{RULES_VERSION}}, updated {{RULES_UPDATED}}. This revision changes registration to October 16–23, sets a project month from October 24 to November 23, moves voting/results to November 24–25, and introduces two categories with one US$200 prize and one vote per participant per category. Other age, solo/new-project, ownership, privacy, reimbursement, claim-period and retention terms remain unchanged.
CyberAlchemy Lab organizes and funds this event. The subscription prize does not represent OpenAI sponsorship or affiliation.
